solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Heavyweight vessel holding whiskey in urban area

indicators.note: the heavyweight and vessel together hold the next letter within them, gripped between their letters

parts.note: a ton is a heavy unit of weight
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a ship is a seagoing vessel

explanation.surface: A heavy ship carrying a cargo of whiskey into a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts W inside TONSHIP, between the O and the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A township is a small town or settled district, an urban area.

clue.text: Some initially talk nonsense, producing razor

indicators.note: initially picks out only the opening letter of the word Some

parts.note: to haver is a Scottish and northern word meaning to babble or talk nonsense

explanation.surface: Some people chatter nonsense and end up producing a razor, as if by magic.
explanation.walkthrough: HAVER, to talk nonsense, is mainly Scottish usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric shaver is a type of razor.

clue.text: Putting up with not having a seat?

definitions.meaning: tolerating, as in 'I can't stand it'
on one's feet rather than seated

explanation.surface: Tolerating something when there is no chair to sit on.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate it, and those without seats are upright on their feet.

clue.text: Benevolent type

definitions.meaning: a sort or category, as in 'of that sort'

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means generous and considerate; the noun means a sort or class.

clue.text: Drawing of ultimately notorious hangman

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word notorious

parts.note: Jack Ketch was a notorious 17th-century English executioner, whose name became slang for a hangman

explanation.surface: A picture of an infamous executioner.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Ketch, executioner under Charles II, was so notorious his name came to mean any hangman.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing.

clue.text: Paint this regularly for an opponent

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the words Paint this, starting with the second

explanation.surface: An instruction to paint something at intervals, for the benefit of a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is against a cause is one of the antis, an opponent of it.

clue.text: See church and northern lake

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: A tourist's itinerary: visit the church and a lake in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A loch is the Scottish word for a lake, so a lake of the north of Britain.

clue.text: Contemplative monarch of slender build

parts.note: someone of slender build is thin
a king is a male monarch

explanation.surface: A thoughtful, slightly built king.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says monarch 'of' slender build, but the answer puts the slender word first.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinking person is reflective or contemplative, given to thought.

clue.text: Bumpy drive finally fenced in by a French priest

indicators.note: fenced in by means the letter is enclosed by the surrounding words' letters

parts.note: un is the French for a
Ven is short for Venerable, the title of an archdeacon

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word drive

explanation.surface: A rough drive, with a French cleric fenced into his parish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fenced in by' puts E inside UNVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An uneven surface is not smooth, so it is bumpy.

clue.text: Arrest Greek character involved in racket

indicators.note: involved in means the Greek letter is wrapped up inside the word for racket

parts.note: din is loud noise, a racket
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek is arrested for involvement in a criminal racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racket' suggests crime, but it means noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain is to hold in custody, synonymous with arrest.

clue.text: Fish in burn?

definitions.meaning: a trout-like freshwater fish of cold lakes
to scorch or blacken by fire

explanation.walkthrough: A burn is also a Scottish stream, where a fish might be found, which is the misleading picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The char is a fish of the salmon family, and to char something is to scorch it.

clue.text: Dubliner possibly misusing his main river at first

indicators.note: misusing the letters means putting them in a wrong, new order
at first takes the opening letter of the word river

explanation.surface: A man from Dublin misusing his main river, the Liffey perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misusing' rearranges HISMAIN with R, the first letter of river.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dubliner is one example of a native of Ireland, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Irish girl joins National Trust — a cause of annoyance

parts.note: Rita is a girl's name
NT is the abbreviation for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: An Irish woman becomes a member of the National Trust and proves a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic houses and land in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritant is anything that irritates, so something that causes annoyance.

clue.text: Turncoat given a job at head of enterprise

parts.note: a post is a position of employment

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of the word enterprise

explanation.surface: A defector rewarded with a senior post at the top of a company.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons a faith or cause, a deserter or turncoat.

clue.text: Vocalist keeping extremely popular type of spaniel

indicators.note: keeping means the word for vocalist holds the other letters within it

parts.note: a vocalist is a singer

indicators.note: extremely takes the outermost letters, first and last, of the word popular

explanation.surface: A singer who keeps a fashionable breed of dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier on popular, but it takes that word's two ends, and 'keeping' sets them inside the vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: The springer is a gundog breed, one kind of spaniel.

clue.text: Young child identified by foot-soldiers leaving railway

indicators.note: leaving means the railway's letters depart from the word for foot-soldiers

parts.note: infantry are soldiers who fight on foot

explanation.surface: A small child spotted by soldiers as they leave a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is a baby or very young child.

clue.text: Academic briefly in favour of opening of faculty

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of

indicators.note: opening of takes the first letter of the word faculty

explanation.surface: A short academic who supports the opening of a new faculty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' says the definition is a shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: Prof is the familiar short form of professor, a senior university academic.

clue.text: Mine includes rising little Scottish shore bird

indicators.note: includes means the word for mine has the other letters set inside it

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: A small Scottish bird nesting on the shore near a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks possessive but is a coal pit; 'rising' turns the Scottish word upwards in this down clue, and 'includes' puts it within.
explanation.definitionFit: The peewit, or lapwing, is a plover often found on shores and fields.

clue.text: Artful youth leader following boat

indicators.note: following means the youth's letter comes after the word for boat

parts.note: craft is a word for a boat or vessel

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of the word youth

explanation.surface: A wily youth leader comes after a boat, like the Artful Dodger.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafty means cunning or wily, synonymous with artful.

clue.text: Australian native beginning to fix top of house

parts.note: a roo is a kangaroo, a native animal of Australia

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of the word fix

explanation.surface: An Aussie local starting to repair the top of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian native' suggests a person, but it is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: The roof is the covering on top of a house.

clue.text: Period of time that's long? Not altogether

indicators.note: not altogether means the word is cut short of its final letter

parts.note: to yearn is to long for something

explanation.surface: A time span that seems long, though not completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' reads as an adjective, but it is the verb, and 'Not altogether' drops the last letter of YEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a twelve-month span of time.

clue.text: Went into beginning and end of Tchaikovsky score

indicators.note: into means the first word goes inside the letters around it
beginning and end of takes the first and last letters of the word Tchaikovsky

explanation.surface: Someone got stuck into the beginning and end of a Tchaikovsky musical score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts WENT inside T and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is a group of twenty.

clue.text: Eg Ben's horse, popular around area

indicators.note: around means the words for horse and popular together go round the letter for area

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: Ben's horse is popular in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: A Ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis; 'Ben's' reads as a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben is a Scottish word for a peak, so Ben Nevis is one example of a high hill.

clue.text: Letter incorporated in Riot Act

indicators.note: incorporated in means the letters sit within the words Riot Act

explanation.surface: A letter that is part of a formal warning to disperse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was a British law proclaimed to order crowds to disperse.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.
